title: Epstein and Axtell's Sugarscape (Appendix B to Izquierdo et al., JASSS 12(1)6)
publisher: JASSS (Journal of Artificial Societies and Social Simulation)

key_points.claim: Sugarscape is a paradigmatic example of the generative approach to social science; it uses heterogeneous autonomous agents competing for renewable resources.
key_points.evidence_quote: a heterogeneous population of autonomous agents compete for renewable resources that are unequally distributed over a 2-dimensional environment

key_points.claim: The model grows in complexity by adding agent activities (sex, culture, trade, combat, disease). Extensions cover norm formation and communication/cooperation.
key_points.evidence_quote: agents are given the ability to engage in new activities such as sex, cultural exchange, trade, combat, disease transmission

key_points.claim: Environment: a 50x50 torus grid with a fixed sugar capacity per cell (two peaks, max 4) and a growback rule at rate α.
key_points.evidence_quote: The environment is a 50×50 grid that wraps around forming a torus.

key_points.claim: Agents have vision, metabolism and max age. They follow a greedy movement rule and are replaced on death (rules M and R).
key_points.evidence_quote: identify the one(s) with the greatest amount of sugar, select the nearest one (randomly if there is more than one), move there and collect all the sugar in it

key_points.claim: Parameterisation for the wealth-distribution model (book p.33): N=250, α=1, vision U[1,6], metabolism U[1,4], initial wealth U[5,25], max age U[60,100].
The Sugarscape model can be formalised as a time-homogeneous Markov chain with a finite state space, so it can be analysed formally.
key_points.evidence_quote: Sugarscape parameterised as indicated above can be represented as a time-homogeneous Markov chain (THMC)

key_points.claim: The chain is proven irreducible and aperiodic (ergodic) using 'regenerating' and 'exterminating pristine' states.
key_points.evidence_quote: This concludes the proof that the induced THMC is irreducible and aperiodic, i.e. ergodic.

key_points.claim: Methodological implication: the long-run distribution of statistics such as wealth is independent of initial conditions. It can be approximated with one long run.
key_points.evidence_quote: we could approximate the limiting distribution of emergent wealth distributions in Sugarscape as much as we like by running just one simulation (with any initial conditions) for long enough

reliability_notes: Full text of a peer-reviewed journal appendix. It covers only chapter 2 of Sugarscape (the basic model), not the later extensions. It is a secondary analysis of the model, not the original book. The proofs are sketched here and are fully developed in the main paper.
